ranked.headline: Inferring single-cell molecular states and lineage structure from tissue images and spatial data
ranked.summary: New preprints decode H&E into molecular and senescence states and separate heritable from niche effects on tumor clones in spatial transcriptomics.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of single-cell molecular state from tissue measurements. Three preprints treat H&E as a molecular readout. Loki2, trained on 15 million cells, tests how much molecular and cellular state routine histology encodes. GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes and maps senescence across aging mouse organs and human skin. sc-HistoMorphomics links 194 nuclear morphometric features to spatial transcriptomics. A newer strand integrates lineage with space. SpOTr uses phylogeny-aware Fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport to place tumor clones onto spots, and SOUR separates heritable from microenvironmental contributions to expression in spatial lineage tracing data. CIRCA recovers identifiable cell and niche programs tied to plaque pathology. Representation learning continues: MCT models cell sets to learn gene co-regulation, and UCE embeddings of 59M+ cells across 614 states map state bridges. Dynamics and integration methods (DRAFT, GatorAnchor) and feedback-network models of heterogeneity restoration form a secondary strand.

ranked.headline: Spatial and epigenetic mapping localizes senescent niches in aging liver and visceral fat
ranked.summary: Several preprints map senescent cells in situ in human and mouse liver and human omental fat, adding p53 perturbation and causal modeling in liver.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is spatially resolved senescence in aging and diseased tissues, concentrated in liver. In human liver, spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq place senescent SenSpots at portal tracts and fibrotic septa, with phenotypes shifting during metabolic liver disease progression. A separate study applies causal discovery machine learning to Visium data to model causes and effects of senescence markers. In aged mouse liver, multi-omic mapping finds senescent cells clustered in inflammatory SenSpots with distinct epigenetic senotypes and zonation. Perturbation evidence comes from mouse liver: p53 loss increases inflammation and metabolic damage, whereas MDM2 inhibitor-driven p53 activation is reported to reverse age-linked changes. Outside liver, human omental adipose from older adults carries more senescent cells than obesity alone explains, involving stem/progenitor and mesothelial cells. Related work links progerin to amplified inflammatory responses in iPSC-derived alveolar cells. Other items address liver injury repair and unrelated topics. All evidence is preprint-stage.

ranked.headline: Automation and cross-modal registration scale quantitative cell mapping in neural tissue
ranked.summary: Preprints pair automated profiling and segmentation with multimodal registration to map neurons, glia, lesions and synaptic interfaces at scale.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is scaling quantitative cell characterization by combining automation with multimodal registration. In Patch-seq, detergent-cleaned reusable pipettes, robotic nucleus extraction and sonication preserve electrophysiology and transcriptomic yield, laying groundwork for automated profiling. Probabilistic C. elegans head-neuron atlases built from near-wild-type strains reach 86.3% top-1 variability-aware identification. Whole-bulb light-sheet expansion microscopy with automated segmentation maps thousands of glomeruli in intact mouse olfactory bulbs. SCOUBI infers axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic transcripts in mouse brain spatial transcriptomics. A second strand integrates imaging modalities. MeXalign coregisters LA-ICP-TOFMS and immunofluorescence via segmentation masks, and FluoMALDI links fluorescence-defined genes, proteins and organelles to spatial lipid composition. Disease- and glia-focused tools add 3D readouts. PASTA resolves amyloid-beta lesion heterogeneity, growth lineages and microglial contacts, and PolyMorph3D quantifies microglia morphology with colocalization of up to four markers. Two methodologically related works lie outside neural tissue: MiSA detects spatial dysbiosis in oral biofilms, and stitched montage cryo-ET maps lamellipodial Arp2/3 actin networks.

ranked.headline: Sequence models and cell-resolved genomics assign noncoding variant effects to cell states
ranked.summary: AlphaGenome 2, lineage-resolved ChromBPNet scoring and the IGVF Catalog knowledge graph push variant interpretation toward cell-type and state resolution.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving regulatory variant effects by cellular context. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-specific regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb sequence across cell states. ChromBPNet models of 17 hematopoietic cell types score 302,830 variants and reveal lineage-structured accessibility effects. The IGVF Catalog integrates 657 variant-effect, regulatory-element and expression datasets into a queryable knowledge graph with API and LLM-agent access. Ancestry adds another axis: in admixed individuals, West African ancestry associates with more allele-specific expression, with 52 replicating loci. Disease-facing frameworks apply context to GWAS loci. EPIC2 links summary statistics to single-cell accessibility, and CAS-X and CELL-X prioritize type 2 diabetes effector genes via multi-tissue eQTLs and islet single-cell data. The endometriosis study cautions that cell-state prioritization depends on marker direction and donor structure. PrediXSKAT, which weights rare coding variants by predicted cis-regulated expression, and CATEomics, a toolkit for treatment-effect estimation, are more peripheral.

ranked.headline: Spatial transcriptomics moves to repeated sampling of living tissue and isoform resolution
ranked.summary: Two needle-array methods, LIFE-seq and LANCE-seq, sample spatial RNA from living tissue repeatedly, while FULL-seq pairs chromatin with full-length transcripts.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is extending transcriptomic resolution in time and in transcript structure. LIFE-seq (nanoforest arrays) and LANCE-seq (encoded microneedle arrays) capture spatial RNA from living tissue without terminating it. LIFE-seq follows cortical injury longitudinally within the same mouse. LANCE-seq profiles mouse brain and tracks APAP-induced liver injury over time. FULL-seq jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and full-length transcripts in single cells, linking promoter regulation to alternative first exon usage. On the analysis side, SpaceMACE adds spatial proximity and expression similarity to tumour-cell annotation. PDAC BioPortal integrates bulk, single-nucleus and spatial PDAC cohorts. A TNBC study combines Perturb-seq CRISPRi responses with TF binding priors for interventional network inference, nominating CTCF, MYC and AP-1 members. The remaining studies apply transcriptomic or epigenetic readouts to specific diseases and tissues rather than adding temporal or isoform resolution: KDM3B-ErbB in cholangiocarcinoma, midkine in PDAC, HPV neuroimmune signatures, and healthy cervical snRNA-seq.

ranked.headline: Nucleic-acid foundation models specialize by taxon, modification, RNA class and design task
ranked.summary: Nine preprints extend sequence foundation models to Plasmodium, methylation, ncRNA and lncRNA, with variant-effect diagnostics and generative regulatory DNA design.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is moving nucleic-acid foundation models from generic pretraining toward specialized inputs, objectives and uses. An apicomplexan model pretrained on 455 assemblies targets regulatory prediction in the data-sparse P. falciparum genome, and ModBERT adds population variants and long-read CpG methylation to pretraining. For RNA, B-RANKO (bidirectional decoder-only ncRNA), LncRFM (structure-guided masking, 24.7M sequences) and MARRI (opening penalties and hybridization gains) encode RNA-specific properties. Evaluation is diagnostic: LAMP links failed personal-genome fine-tuning to distal sequence, and Borzoi and AlphaGenome are compared with variant-based methods in admixed Latino individuals. GENECraft and REGAL use these models for controllable regulatory DNA and enhancer design, REGAL with cross-species validation. All nine are preprints, so the claims remain unreviewed.

ranked.headline: Transcription factors, chromatin marks and splicing tune ABA, JA and cytokinin-auxin outputs
ranked.summary: New plant studies map regulators of ABA, JA and bud-outgrowth hormones to specific promoters, histone marks, splice events and miRNA targets.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is regulatory control of hormone biosynthesis, catabolism and sensitivity at defined genomic or transcript targets. ABA is the most frequent node: GhNAC029 represses GhNCED1 in cotton, RhWUS1 represses RhNCED3 in rose, methylation of the BraCYP707A3.A02 promoter blocks BraBPC2.A08 binding in Brassica, and SRPKII-SR45 control of HAB1 splicing shapes ABA sensitivity in Arabidopsis. ANAC030 promotes senescence through JA synthesis, and RSI1/FLD demethylates H3K4me2/3 at its own TSS to self-limit pathogen-induced expression. The miR159a-BrMYB12 module acts on raffinose-pathway genes for heat tolerance, and maize H2A.Z mapping provides chromatin context for tissue-specific expression. New is the resolution to specific promoters, epigenetic marks, splice events and miRNA targets.

ranked.headline: ROS, H2S and antioxidant pathways act through defined protein modules in plant development and stress
ranked.summary: New Arabidopsis, apple, pear and soybean studies map redox signals onto specific protein modules controlling stomata, germination, photoprotection and fruit traits.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is redox chemistry acting through defined protein modules rather than as nonspecific damage. In Arabidopsis, peroxisomal H2O2 homeostasis under PEG-induced water stress rebalances ABA and GA metabolism, slowing seed germination. 2-Cys peroxiredoxins interact with FAD7/FAD8 to raise trienoic fatty acids in phosphatidylglycerol and aid PSII recovery from high light. H2S persulfidation and PRMT5-dependent LSm4 methylation connect H2S signaling to alternative splicing in stomatal closure. In apple, MxMPK4-1 phosphorylates MxME3-7 at S201, enhancing ROS signaling under iron deficiency. In pear, PUB8 targets ZAT11/12 for degradation, while ZAT11/12 activate LAC1 to drive ROS-linked lignin polymerization in stone cells. Ascorbate regulation by MdMYB70/MdbHLH62 in fresh-cut apple, melatonin plus selenium nanoparticles in soybean, and an SOD review are related but less module-centered.

ranked.headline: Stress remodels organelles via selective autophagy, tethers, condensates and trafficking checkpoints
ranked.summary: New work links distinct adaptors, tethers and condensates to organelle quality control under starvation, iron loss and lysosomal damage.
ranked.synthesis: Most items describe organelle remodeling under stress through autophagy or related quality-control routes, but the compartments, stresses and effectors differ. Contact-phagy uses SIGMAR1-CCPG1 to turn over ER-mitochondria contact-site subdomains. Iron deficiency drives pexophagy via GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1 and TFEB/TFE3 activation. Yeast Mdm1 balances phospholipid and neutral lipid metabolism to allow autophagosome completion. Processing bodies and stress granules support lysosomal quality after damage, while RAB11-RAB30 uses phosphoinositide turnover for endosomal remodeling and survival. NRF2-dependent autophagy clears lipofuscin-like granules in RPE cells, and the axon initial segment gates lysosome trafficking via MCF2L. The GCase-deficiency study adds impaired macropinocytic uptake of α-synuclein ectosomes by astrocytes. What is new is the assignment of specific adaptors, tethers and condensates to each context, not a single shared mechanism.

ranked.headline: Genetic and pathological perturbations converge on dysregulated dopaminergic and cholinergic control of striatum
ranked.summary: Eight preprints link risk genes, DAT variants, D1 loss and α-synuclein to altered striatal dopamine signaling and behavior across psychiatric and Parkinson's models.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is altered dopaminergic and cholinergic control of striatal output across neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative models. Tshz3 deletion in cholinergic neurons reduces M1 muscarinic transmission onto projection neurons and abolishes D1 versus D2 excitability differences. The 3q29 deletion model shows elevated evoked dorsal striatal dopamine release via PKC-mediated mechanisms. Functional profiling of 55 SLC6A3 missense variants from psychiatric patients resolves seven phenotypic classes. In 6-OHDA mice, prolonged D1 signaling loss makes direct-pathway neurons hyperresponsive to dopamine. α-Synuclein overexpression in midbrain dopamine neurons produces progressive action-outcome learning deficits, and an Anxa1-associated human dopaminergic population is most depleted in Parkinson's brains. Aralar/AGC1 loss links dopaminergic and redox dysfunction to impaired sociability, rescued by β-hydroxybutyrate. The 5-HT2A deletion study addresses a separate serotonergic and hippocampal axis. All items are preprints.

ranked.headline: DREAM and post-transcriptional controls restrict fate and cell-cycle programs in early development
ranked.summary: New C. elegans, Drosophila, Xenopus and zebrafish studies link DREAM repression, translation control and phosphorylation to narrowing developmental competence.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how regulatory layers constrain developmental competence and cell-cycle programs. In C. elegans, blastomeres stay competent for muscle fate until late 16E, with LIN-54/DREAM and MET-2 restricting plasticity. DREAM also represses zen-4, cyk-4 and spd-1 at the intestinal transition to endomitosis, blocking cytokinesis. Post-transcriptional and post-translational control appear elsewhere: Bicaudal-C silences translation through CCR4-NOT, Lsm14, 4E-T and Ddx6 in Xenopus axis patterning; CDK1-MAPK sites are dephosphorylated by Calcineurin at Drosophila egg activation; and -1 frameshifting generates a neural stem cell Zelda proteoform with tissue-specific pioneer activity. New here is DREAM acting on both fate and cytokinetic gene programs. Zebrafish M rRNA transcription is excluded as a female sex determinant, and rRNA biogenesis disruption causes histone mRNA misprocessing in C. elegans.

ranked.headline: Haploblocks, polygenic parallelism and contingency govern outcomes of rapid adaptation under stress
ranked.summary: New preprints link genomic architecture to evolutionary rescue, extinction and invasion, and test how well genomic predictions capture adaptive limits.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how genomic architecture and contingency determine whether populations adapt fast enough to persist. In cowpea seed beetles, rapid, repeatable rescue on lentil relies on large non-recombining haploblocks on chromosomes 1 and 9. In outdoor Drosophila under insecticide, half of the populations went extinct despite strong parallel polygenic adaptation, while pre-adaptation prevented extinction. Copepod salinity adaptation shows polygenic divergence along the Baltic gradient, with genomic offsets limited as predictors of physiological range. Boechera stricta analyses suggest projected hot, dry climates may exceed adaptive capacity. Drosophila suzukii invasion is tested for seasonal adaptive tracking, and stickleback introductions are predicted better by source population identity than by environmental matching. Simulations add that reproductive competition reduces genetic load. New here is the joint weighing of structural variation, polygenic parallelism, contingency and predictive limits.

ranked.headline: Theory links epistasis, plasticity and structure to fitness dynamics, coexistence and host-parasite evolution
ranked.summary: New theory extends fitness landscape, epistasis and coexistence frameworks to dynamics across environments, population structure, space and mutation rate evolution.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a theoretical focus on how fitness is structured and how that structure shapes evolutionary trajectories. A review frames evolution as fitness landscape navigation, relating epistasis, ruggedness and accessibility. A global epistasis model fitted to yeast data predicts how non-home fitness changes during adaptation across backgrounds and environments. A multi-locus model finds that mutation rates evolve through indirect selection out of equilibrium and are selected against under homogenising selection. Two coexistence-theory preprints add within-population structure and competition-induced plasticity to niche and fitness differences. Host-parasite models show that spatial network topology and costs shape resistance and infectivity, and that parasite-impaired host mobility favours reduced virulence. The common move is from equilibrium fitness values toward context-dependent dynamics.

ranked.headline: Cell-type and stage-resolved omics map early molecular lesions in neurodegeneration models
ranked.summary: Preprints resolve proteomic, transcriptomic and variant-function changes by cell type, age and stage in Huntington's, ALS, Parkinson's-linked and FMRP-loss models.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving molecular pathology by cell type, age or disease stage. In R6/1 mice, cell-type-resolved proteomics shows synaptic protein loss in excitatory neurons before motor onset, with reduced neuronal-support proteins in glia. TgHD minipig putamen shows age-dependent transcript and protein changes, including reduced D2 neuron markers. Fmr1-KO profiling reports cell type-specific remodelling of excitatory and inhibitory synapses. In ALS-related work, a TDP-43 APEX2 atlas shows interactome changes persisting beyond stress granule clearance, younger ALS donors carry higher neuronal somatic mutation burden with an SBS5 signature, and SETX loss has stage-dependent effects in iPSC motor neurons. A multiplexed assay maps function for over 10,400 GBA1 variants, and Ankle2-VRK1 work links proteostasis to neuronal resilience in Drosophila. Not all items address neurodegeneration directly.

ranked.headline: Perturbation-response models are being benchmarked and rebuilt around noise, concordance and interaction structure
ranked.summary: Cross-source discordance in drug transcriptomes and new benchmark metrics make noise-aware, rigorously evaluated perturbation-response models a pressing need.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that perturbation-response prediction is being constrained by data quality and evaluation design. A comparison of six drug-perturbation transcriptomic resources reports high treated-expression agreement but limited cross-source concordance of drug-induced responses. The Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 defines six metrics for zero-shot CRISPRi response prediction. Methods respond with explicit noise or structure handling: DeepCINET models viability assay noise, siGMA uses heteroscedastic uncertainty for noisy cross-dataset siRNA efficacy labels, GFM adds knowledge graphs to latent flow matching for unseen Perturb-seq genes, GAIN learns interactions over an additive baseline for combinatorial perturbations, and CIRCE infers graded signaling activity from combinatorial perturbation structure. PTM-BDL extends drug-response prediction to site-resolved phosphosite features.

ranked.headline: Trait evolution decouples from species boundaries and varies with demography, ecology and sexual selection
ranked.summary: New lineage-level studies test how drift, gene flow, niche lability and sexual selection shape phenotypic and species diversification across plants, birds, lizards and insects.
ranked.synthesis: Across plants, birds, lizards, butterflies and insects, these studies link phenotypic divergence to diversification but show that the link is uneven and context dependent. Mimosa clades span a continuum of diversification rates, with radiations contributing most diversity and disparity and tied to abiotic niche lability. In island kingfishers, faster plumage color evolution tracks faster diversification and accelerates as genomic diversity declines, consistent with drift. Bark anoles show convergent signaling traits decoupled from genomic species boundaries, with gene flow shaping speciation outcomes. Iridescent dichromatism across 3,151 bird species is explained by both Darwinian and Wallacean processes, and sexual dimorphism in leaf-footed bugs is labile. Masked owls and Heliconius cydno add genomic evidence of divergence tied to phenotype, island isolation and Andean geography. The common advance is testing trait evolution directly against genomic and demographic parameters.

ranked.headline: Higher genomic and phylogenetic resolution is reshaping ecological inference across environmental microbiomes
ranked.summary: New preprints show long-read assembly, MAG recovery and pangenomics changing which taxa and functions are inferred across sludge, sediment and polar ocean systems.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that resolution of genomic and phylogenetic structure shapes ecological interpretation. HiFi long-read metagenomics of activated sludge recovers denitrifiers, nitrifiers and Accumulibacter missed by short-read assemblies, biasing N2O-related inferences. Great Barrier Reef sediments yield 2,698 MAGs, mostly novel, with notable metabolic heterogeneity. The Micromonas polaris pangenome resolves two cryptic ecotypes and 990 polar-specific genes, and metaEukaryome detects eukaryotic bycatch in 75,727 metagenomes. Amplicon-based studies add context at coarser resolution: marble biofilms show taxonomic turnover with conserved phylogenetic structure, river microeukaryotes track water chemistry, and octocoral microbiomes are host-specific and stable over three years. The systems and methods differ, and only some of the work is genome-resolved.

ranked.headline: Locus-restricted histone methylation silencing is traced to specific recruitment and protection mechanisms
ranked.summary: Seven new reports across five taxa resolve how H3K4, H3K9 and H3K27 methylation are targeted to or shielded from specific loci.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how histone methylation is directed to, or excluded from, particular loci. For H3K27me3, maternal Foxh1 recruits PRC2/Ezh2 in Xenopus, PRC2 shapes parent-of-origin PHE1 binding at Arabidopsis imprinted genes, and CAF-1 supports PRC2-dependent silencing in Neurospora facultative heterochromatin. In mouse ES cells, H3K4 methylation and DNA methylation cooperatively protect regulatory elements from Polycomb. For H3K4me1, Pol II Ser2P redistribution into gene bodies recruits the FLD-LD demethylase complex to license silencing in Arabidopsis. For H3K9, IDC, STWL and PZG recruit SETDB1 via WDE to phf7 in Drosophila, and EHMT1/2 time cortical neurogenesis through H3K9me2-dependent and -independent mechanisms. The new elements are defined recruiters, licensing steps and protective cooperation at individual loci.

ranked.headline: Brain function is framed as state-dependent, distributed dynamics over a shared structural scaffold
ranked.summary: Seven fMRI and EEG preprints link cognitive state, trait dynamics and sensory precision to distributed, low-dimensional brain organization rather than fixed modules.
ranked.synthesis: The preprints treat brain organization as distributed and state-dependent rather than modular. Structure-function coupling varies with cognitive state, strongest during movie-watching and weakest under working memory load. Resting-state fMRI from 994 HCP participants links spatial and temporal network organization to trait-like dynamics. A meta-analysis of 912 papers finds no single core for self-related processing, describing shifting coalitions of systems. Oddball detection follows a shared low-dimensional state landscape with modality-dependent later trajectories. Information decomposition of film-viewing fMRI maps storage, transfer and transformation, and a signed dynamic connectivity framework relates subcortical routing to network flexibility and behavioral traits. EEG work ties sensory representational precision to alpha power, pupil dilation and correlated noise. New here is the emphasis on dynamic, low-dimensional state descriptions, often from naturalistic paradigms.

ranked.headline: Neural models learn cell-state representations from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics
ranked.summary: Seven preprints apply transformers, autoencoders and equivariant networks to cell embeddings, spatial inference and population discovery across modalities.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is learning cell-state representations with deep models across scales and data types. Foundation-style models include scUNVEIL, pretrained on about 92 million human cells with next-UMI prediction, and Bloom, a transformer trained on 300,000 mouse brain cells that unifies expression and chromatin accessibility. Spatial work either resolves subcellular organization, using a rotation-equivariant network on 3D transcript embeddings, or deconvolves multicellular spots into single-cell profiles with st2sc. Other items address cohort structure, with scPACE modeling donor and cell states and imputing missing cell types, and de novo population discovery by combining clustering with fine-tuned Geneformer outputs. One preprint extends the theme to imaging, predicting cell movement from images to improve LAP-based tracking by 2.7 to 5.7 percentage points.

ranked.headline: Protein and RNA predictors are tested for what their outputs really encode
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test protein and RNA predictors against curated annotations, chemical probing data and conformational ensembles.
ranked.synthesis: Across these preprints, the common thread is whether predictor outputs are checked against independent biological reference data. The interpretability study tests ESMC probe, neuron and layer conclusions against residue-level curated annotations and reports that these conclusions depend on the method applied. MXfold2 is extended to learn RNA secondary structure from chemical probing data using implicit maximum-likelihood training. MANTA separates geometric prior estimation from coordinate generation for intrinsically disordered protein ensembles and identifies prior estimation as the main bottleneck. DynamicsPLM adds molecular dynamics heads to a 35M-parameter protein language model for zero-shot mutation effect prediction. Region-aware pooling of mRNA foundation model embeddings improves linear probe performance over global mean pooling. FoldMapper and A2Holo extend structure-based design and apo-to-holo conformational transition prediction. The new element is less a single method than a shift toward validating representations and predictions against curated, experimental or dynamical references.

ranked.headline: Combined stresses reshape chromatin, hormone and clock control of plant heat responses
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a proteomics study examine how heat combines with drought, phosphate starvation and clock genes to shape plant stress responses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is how plants integrate heat with other stresses through chromatin, hormone and clock regulation. In potato, combined heat and drought alter chromatin accessibility and prime ABA biosynthesis through StNCED3 on repeated exposure. In rice, thermopriming yields a restrained, lower-entropy heat transcriptional response with H3K27me3 retention and memory chaperone expression. In Arabidopsis, combined heat and phosphate starvation produces organ-specific jasmonate changes, with JA-Ile rising in roots and JA falling in shoots. Clock-focused work in Arabidopsis links CCA1 and LHY to time-of-day heat responses across transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic layers, and a proteomics study of rve4 6 8 mutants connects clock genes to osmotic and salt stress responses. What is new is the emphasis on priming and organ-level divergence under stress combinations, though the clock and salt-stress studies address related but distinct stress contexts.

ranked.headline: Cell-type-resolved omics dissect Alzheimer's models and human cortical disease
ranked.summary: Cell-type-resolved transcriptomic and multi-omic resources now enable cross-study comparison of Alzheimer's disease mechanisms in mice and humans.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is cell-type-resolved omics applied to Alzheimer's disease (AD) models and human brain. A 5xFAD snRNA-seq atlas finds VIP interneurons most disrupted in synapse programs and preferentially rescued by rolipram, implicating a Pde7b/CREB1 cAMP axis. A harmonized resource of 1,863 uniformly processed mouse cortex and hippocampus transcriptomes, including AD models, enables cross-study comparison. Lysosomal biogenesis (MiT/TFE) is reported to precede and couple to disease-associated microglia reprogramming across murine injury, amyloidosis and human AD. A meta-analysis of 1,738 human cortices links cortical miRNAs, notably miR-132-3p, to tau pathology. Developmental regulatory maps from 231 prefrontal cortices and the VEGABrain visualization tool add developmental context. The preeclampsia miRNA-mRNA study is peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Engineered protein interfaces steer degradation, binding and signaling outcomes
ranked.summary: Rational design of molecular glues, antibody conjugates and binders now targets transient interfaces with improved selectivity control.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is deliberate engineering of protein-protein interfaces to control target fate or activity. Two molecular glue degrader preprints illustrate this: TrIP-MGRD targets transient PPI pockets, supported by a CDK12-DDB1 cryo-EM structure and the glue C432, while an antibody-drug conjugate of a CCNK glue degrader gives HER2-selective cyclin K degradation in breast cancer. A degron-informed study identifies DCAF10 as a targeted protein degradation E3 ligase, with an optimized Pr-GFI recruiter degrading FKBP12 and BRD9. Computational design extends the theme to PDZ-binding peptides in a shared latent space, MobGen monobodies against SARS-CoV-2 Spike RBD, and a quantum-mechanics-guided covalent recruiter of FBXO22 for BRD4 degradation. Paired deep mutational scanning of Lck yields a nilotinib-sensitized variant. The new element is rational, selective, interface-aware design, though modalities and maturity differ across items.

ranked.headline: Regulators sustain germline gene expression, transposon silencing and gamete fitness
ranked.summary: Single-cell, spatial and genetic screens now link germline, meiotic and ovarian regulators to transposon control and gamete quality.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how specific regulators sustain gene expression programs and genome integrity during gametogenesis. In mouse germ cells, COPS5 loss downregulates piRNA pathway genes, reduces pachytene piRNAs, activates LINE1 and IAP transposons, and arrests spermatogenesis. In budding yeast gametogenesis, Hsf1, Skn7, Msn2 and Msn4 are active without external stress, and the antioxidant genes TSA1 and AHP1 protect gametes. In Drosophila, Marf1 is newly expressed in the male accessory gland and integrates into its gene regulatory network, while GAR1 regulates lipid storage, development, sgg splicing and PI3K/AKT signaling. Single-cell and spatial multi-omics of human ovaries across menopause implicate HEYL in ovarian aging and senescence, and a yeast synthetic genetic array screen links nuclear genes to mitochondrial COX2 expression via Rim101 signaling. These last two extend the scope beyond germline silencing.

ranked.headline: Elicitor perception links SYR1, SOBIR1 and CPK13 to plant immune outputs
ranked.summary: Recent work identifies new elicitors and receptor-dependent immune outputs in wheat, Nicotiana and Arabidopsis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how plants detect elicitors and convert recognition into immune outputs. In Nicotiana, four newly described bioactive systemins are perceived by SlSYR1, and a premature stop codon in SYR1 orthologs of LAB N. benthamiana accounts for lineage-specific systemin insensitivity. The Ustilaginoidea virens secreted protein UvWSC1 acts as a virulence factor and immune elicitor, triggering OsCPK13- and SOBIR1-dependent cell death. Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) HC-Pro triggers ADR1/NRG1-dependent hypersensitive cell death in N. benthamiana, modulated by P3N-PIPO interaction. N-hydroxypipecolic acid is reported to trigger systemic acquired resistance against wheat leaf rust. In Arabidopsis, UGT74F1 and UGT74F2 restrict turnip mosaic virus through a mechanism independent of salicylic acid, jasmonate and RNA silencing. The mild SCMV-based maize vector is a methodological tool and is peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Structural and simulation studies dissect protein binding, transport and ion coupling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply MD, crystallography and AlphaFold3 to resolve binding sites, selectivity and coupling in membrane transporters and disordered regions.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how binding partners and permeant ions are recognised and discriminated at defined sites in proteins, using combined simulation, structural and functional approaches. Nanobody mapping of the BasC transporter reveals a bias toward the intracellular cavity, while enhanced-sampling simulations resolve the multimodal landscape by which the FCP1 disordered region folds on binding Rap74. In SERT, Na+ occupancy of the Na2 site is reported to couple sodium to serotonin transport through TM1, TM5 and TM8 interactions, and in XPR1, phosphate selectivity arises from direct multi-ion competition in the pore. Among solute-binding proteins, three divergent members share a conserved loss of affinity for perfluorinated ligands, with locally tunable sensitivity to partial fluorination. The HIV-1 integrase study adds an evolutionary perspective, showing that drug-resistance mutations shift folding stability and catalytic geometry only marginally.

ranked.headline: Learned models predict phosphosites, enzyme kcat, ADMET and catalytic residues
ranked.summary: Preprints now couple protein language models, 3D structure and conformal uncertainty to predict PTM sites, kcat, ADMET and docking error.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is supervised prediction of molecular and residue-level properties from sequence, structure and learned representations, applied to protein function, enzyme kinetics, peptide pharmacokinetics and ligand binding. HieraPTM and SCOPE combine sequence, evolutionary or language-model features with 3D structural context to localize functional sites, with SCOPE reporting mutagenesis validation. EnzRef addresses kcat by modeling reactants and products separately against a frozen protein language model, while AIO targets ADMET of cyclic peptides and macrocycles with segment-level attribution for interpretability. BrainRoute pairs BBB permeability prediction (external balanced accuracy 0.659) with community verification, and the conformal framework quantifies 3D docking uncertainty with dependence-aware intervals. The new element is the emphasis on calibrated uncertainty and interpretability layered onto these predictors.

ranked.headline: Transposable elements shape aging adipose tissue and neuronal genome dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply single-cell and long-read sequencing to map transposable element activity in aging tissues, organoids and human neurons.
ranked.synthesis: Across these preprints, the dominant thread is the activity and genomic consequences of transposable elements in somatic tissues. In aging female mouse and human visceral adipose tissue, snRNA-seq shows retrotransposon upregulation in human aging. In the brain, LUSTRE maps L1 retrotransposition sites in about 17,600 adult human neurons to estimate somatic insertion rates. Single-cell long-read sequencing of cortical organoids links locus-resolved, human-specific transposable elements to the timing of the radial glia-to-neuron transition, supported by CRISPRi manipulation. What is new is resolution at the single-cell and locus level in human tissue. A separate study estimates neuronal point mutation rates of about 25.9 per diploid genome per year, similar in mice and humans. The remaining two items, an enhancer reporter platform in iPSC-derived organoids and Sanger verification of a Prnp-Prnd deletion junction, are methodological rather than transposon-focused.

ranked.headline: Computational workflows for microbial genomics, amplicon profiling and reproducibility
ranked.summary: New preprints extend reproducible software for microbial genomics and amplicon data to species-level resolution and private deployment.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is accessible, reproducible computational tooling for microbial genomics and amplicon profiling. VPHYL converts Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s nanopore 16S abundance tables into phyloseq and BIOM objects. RADSuite pairs a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database with RADx to enable species-level microbiome identification. nf-core/pairgenomealign offers a scalable Nextflow pipeline using LAST for pairwise whole-genome alignment, and Sparrowhawk delivers private, in-browser microbial genomics via WebAssembly. Two items extend the theme to other settings: MAUDE-Py reimplements pooled CRISPR screen analysis in Python with faster runtime and near-identical results, and a Fusion transpiling study tests functional identity of SNHA code across nine languages. What is new is primarily at the tool level, namely workflow design, interoperability and privacy-preserving deployment, rather than new biological findings.

ranked.headline: Developmental and environmental perturbations reshape glial and neuronal states in vivo
ranked.summary: Preprints and one published study dissect cell-type-specific neural responses to developmental, immune, and aging perturbations in vivo.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is cell-type-resolved readout of neural tissue after a defined perturbation. In mice, neonatal SARS-CoV-2 spike protein exposure altered SOX2 cells and TBR1 neurons at P10 in a region-specific manner, without broad cerebrovascular or blood-brain barrier changes. Maternal TPOAb exposure in mice, reported in a published study, produced placental inflammation, fetal BBB disruption, hippocampal microglial activation, and altered BDNF and synaptic signaling. An enriched environment increased prefrontal perineuronal nets via NRG1/ErbB4 signaling and aggrecan in adult mice, with improved cognition. A multi-omic, spatially resolved atlas of spinal cord aging in mice and humans links senescence markers to specific cell types. Isogenic NGLY1-deficient human iPSC-derived models, which are not in vivo, show elevated RUNX1 and altered microglial development, phagocytosis, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. What is new is the resolution of these readouts at cell-type level, although most of the evidence remains at preprint stage.

ranked.headline: Long-read genome assembly of red seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis reported
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study extend genomic, epigenetic and viral characterization of marine algae and their associated viruses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is the genomic and genetic characterization of algae and their viruses, with attention to genome architecture, epigenetic machinery and viral communities. A de novo long-read reference genome of the red seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis provides an assembly of 918.2 Mb across 149 contigs, with 6100 annotated genes and 90.5% repetitive sequence. In kelps (Laminariales), native-DNA nanopore sequencing detected no nuclear DNA methylation, supporting a predicted loss of canonical methyltransferases in brown algae. Viral studies extend this picture: an RNA virome from New Zealand intertidal kelp revealed novel viral lineages, with higher viral diversity at a city-proximal site and in unhealthy kelp, while long-read metagenomics of mesopelagic Andaman Sea seawater yielded 1,604 high-confidence viral contigs, mostly bacteriophages. Population-genetic work on the snow alga Chlainomonas sp. indicates a haploid-diploid life cycle with clonal reproduction and likely high selfing. What is new is the application of long-read and single-cell approaches to non-model algal and viral systems.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale phylogenomics resolves discordance from ILS, introgression and data density
ranked.summary: Genome-wide datasets now test whether gene tree discordance reflects incomplete lineage sorting, introgression, or insufficient resolution.
ranked.synthesis: Across these preprints and one peer-reviewed study, genome-scale data are used to resolve relationships where gene trees and organellar or nuclear signals disagree. In Australian Gossypium, whole-genome phylogenomics finds plastid-nuclear discordance but little nuclear evidence of introgression, which revisits homoploid hybrid speciation. In Dipsacales, whole-genome resequencing of 88 species resolves Linnina backbone relationships and attributes discordance to incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) and possible ancient gene flow. In Aizoaceae, phylotranscriptomics shows that gene-dense data resolve major relationships, while short internodes limit resolution within the rapid radiation. Flatfish whole-genome phylogenomics and synteny support a single origin of body-plan asymmetry. What is new is the emphasis on data density and genomic context, with the ice plant result marking limits on what gene-dense data can resolve.

ranked.headline: Cellular states in 22q11.2 deletion link to variable schizophrenia penetrance
ranked.summary: Preprints now connect 22q11.2 deletion to neuronal, glial and barrier cell-state differences tied to variable schizophrenia penetrance.
ranked.synthesis: Three preprints on 22q11.2 deletion carriers or deletion models examine cellular compartments in relation to variable schizophrenia penetrance. In iPSC-derived neurons from carriers, schizophrenia is associated with impaired neuronal mitophagy and lysosomal acidity, and the defect is described as reversible. In iPSC-derived blood-brain barrier cells from carriers, structural and metabolic differences are linked to penetrance. In a 22q11.2 deletion mouse model, prefrontal cortex at P28 shows increased immature and mature oligodendrocytes alongside reduced myelination. The new element is the association of penetrance-linked differences with specific cellular states across neuronal, glial and barrier compartments. The cntnap2-/- autism, PLX5622 Purkinje cell and LKB1 granule cell studies address other models and are not attributed to the deletion.

ranked.headline: Haplotype and pangenome frameworks resolve allele-specific, reference-dependent variation
ranked.summary: Haplotype-resolved long-read and pangenome references now reveal allele-specific expression and reference-dependent biology in crop genomes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is that genotype-linked measurements depend on the genetic and reference framework used to interpret them. In heat-stressed tetraploid potato, long-read RNA-seq resolves haplotype-specific expression, identifying a heat-inducible allele and a nucleus-targeted HSP40 isoform. A parent-of-origin-resolved Granny Smith apple genome shows that matched references reveal sun-exposure and cold-storage responses that other references miss. In Capsicum, a 48-genome super-pangenome reveals structural variation and the genetic basis of carotenoid and capsaicinoid diversity, while a pangenome-guided k-mer GWAS links pungency and aroma terpene traits to Pun1 haplotypes and TPS genes. Switchgrass field mapping of eQTL and GxE effects and pearl millet ionomic stability under drought are related but less directly tied to this framework. What is new is the use of haplotype-resolved and pangenome frameworks to resolve allele-specific and reference-dependent variation.

ranked.headline: Mitochondrial carriers and dynamics shape branched-chain and fatty acid metabolism
ranked.summary: Five preprints converge on mitochondrial import, dynamics and fatty acid oxidation across muscle, liver, adipose and immune cells.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that mitochondrial substrate entry and organelle remodeling set tissue metabolic output. Two preprints identify SLC25A35 as the mitochondrial carrier for branched-chain keto acids (BCKAs). One of them also names MCT1 and MCT2 as cellular entry transporters and reports that import limits hepatic BCKA handling, while the other links BCKA uptake to adipocyte lipogenesis and fatty acid metabolism. MTCH2 supports mitochondrial metabolic remodeling, respiration and fatty acid oxidation in muscle satellite cells. Myeloid mDIC deletion shifts adipose macrophages toward an efferocytosis-associated state while preserving mitochondrial respiration. In KPC cachexia mice, muscle OPA1 overexpression or BNIP3 knockdown partly preserved muscle mass and function in a sex-dependent manner. Dual Hadha and Hadhb mRNA delivery restores fatty acid oxidation in a trifunctional protein deficiency model. The new element is the transporter-level account of BCKA import, linking cellular uptake to mitochondrial entry.

ranked.headline: Stromal cell states and matrix-remodelling programmes across human tissues and disease
ranked.summary: Single-nucleus, chromatin and long-read profiling now resolve stromal states and matrix-remodelling cores across human tissues and disease.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how stromal cells are defined by their states and by the matrix-remodelling programmes they carry. In human atrial fibrillation, single-nucleus multi-omics identifies fibroblast states and implicates JMJD1C in TGF-beta-driven fibroblast remodelling. In healthy synovium and infrapatellar fat pad, paired bulk, single-nucleus RNA and chromatin accessibility profiling describes a continuous stromal continuum rather than discrete populations. Cross-organ analysis of human and mouse fibrosis RNA-seq data identifies a conserved 25-gene matrix-remodelling core, although gene-level cross-species concordance is weak. Human stromal clones with high bone-forming capacity share HIPPO competency signatures and oxidative metabolism. What is new is the combination of single-nucleus and chromatin-level profiling with cross-organ comparison, while the conserved core remains weakly concordant between species. The heart isoform atlas and bovine MSC culture transcriptomics address adjacent questions and do not directly examine stromal matrix control.

ranked.headline: Preservation and sequencing choices shape molecular biodiversity inference from samples
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test how seawater storage and specimen-based sequencing affect molecular biodiversity estimates from eDNA and museum material.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread in this set is molecular inference of biodiversity from environmental samples and specimens. A freezing experiment on seawater samples reports that one month of storage lowered eDNA-inferred marine invertebrate richness and altered community composition, with Pseudocalanus copepods among the notably affected taxa, pointing to preservation as a source of bias in metabarcoding estimates. A Cook Inlet time series applies eDNA metabarcoding and qPCR to track endangered beluga whale occurrence alongside salmonid and eulachon prey dynamics. Nanopore barcoding of 3,657 European Ulva samples identifies 46 species from 30 countries, and nanopore mini-barcoding recovers COI sequences from century-old spider museum specimens. What is new is direct attention to sampling protocol effects and to multi-taxon eDNA time series, alongside low-input genotyping of zebra mussel veligers via multiple displacement amplification.

ranked.headline: Sound responses in fish and tunicates vary by individual, life stage and season
ranked.summary: Preprints and a published study show that aquatic animal responses to sound depend on individual, life stage and season rather than being fixed.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these items is that sound responses in aquatic organisms are not a single fixed trait but vary among individuals, life stages and seasons. In zebrafish, emergence latency differed among individuals and shortened across two tests, and sound exposure reduced vertical midline crossings more than ambient sound did. In Oikopleura dioica, anthropogenic noise altered behaviour in a stage- and signal-specific way, with larvae appearing most sensitive. In Arctic cod, auditory evoked potential measurements showed seasonal differences in hearing sensitivity between spawning and non-spawning fish. The new element is the explicit treatment of individual, life-stage and seasonal variation as components of sound responses. Only the Arctic cod study is published; the zebrafish and Oikopleura findings are preprints and remain provisional.

ranked.headline: Regulatory feedback tunes TH17 differentiation and interferon responses in immune cells
ranked.summary: Three preprints show that metabolic, signaling-history and transcription-factor states calibrate later immune and epithelial responses beyond acute stimuli.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is that intrinsic regulatory states, rather than acute stimuli alone, calibrate the magnitude and direction of differentiation or interferon output. Pharmacologic IRE1 activation promotes HMGCR degradation and reduces intracellular cholesterol biosynthesis, which suppresses TH17 differentiation. In primary human macrophages, prior cytokine exposure constrains later transcriptional responses, with IFNβ dominating. In mice, the intestinal epithelial factor HNF4α restrains baseline interferon signaling and is required for full interferon induction during Salmonella infection. What is new is the mechanistic link between a metabolic enzyme and TH17 fate, together with evidence that signaling history and transcription-factor identity set how subsequent responses are calibrated. The HNF4α study applies the same regulatory logic to an epithelial factor rather than an immune mechanism.
